messages:
jess (customer): hitting 403 on POST /v1/generate for customer=acme-inc. curl returns 403 and body 'permission_denied'. request-id in headers: rr-6b2f4c9a. can someone help?

maya (support): sorry about that — can you paste the curl you ran (redact token) and the full response headers? 403 usually means token scope or org mismatch.

jess (customer): here you go (redacted):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"hello"}'
```
response headers:
```
HTTP/2 403
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: rr-6b2f4c9a
date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:05:10 GMT
content-length: 86
```
body: {"error":"permission_denied","message":"token does not have access to requested org"}

rory (eng-support): thanks. that message suggests the API key is scoped to a different project/org. can you confirm which org the customer is using in the dashboard? if they have multiple orgs it's common to accidentally use a project-scoped key.

jess (customer): customer says org id is org_911. in dashboard the key shows as 'service-key (project-level)'.

maya (support): ok likely cause. quick repro steps for you to try and for us to validate: 1) try the same curl with an org-scoped key (org key or org token), 2) add header `X-Org-ID: org_911` to see if that unblocks, 3) run with `-v` to capture the TLS handshake and final headers. please paste the new x-request-id if it changes.

jess (customer): will try. one question — how do we get an org-scoped key?

rory (eng-support): org keys are generated via the dashboard > Org Settings > API keys. if customer cannot create one (permissions) they need an org admin to create it. alternately we can create a short-lived token server-side for repro.

jess (customer): tried adding header `X-Org-ID: org_911` and using same key, response still 403, new request id rr-6b2f51f2.

maya (support): thanks — could you run this exact command (include -v and --trace-ascii) so we can see request/response wire details?
```
curl -i -v --trace-ascii - -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_911" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"hello"}'
```
please paste the trace output and the x-request-id header value. redact any token pieces.

jess (customer): pasted trace to thread (redacted). trace shows TLS OK, then HTTP/2 reset before body sometimes. headers include `x-request-id: rr-6b2f51f2`. body still permission_denied.

rory (eng-support): thanks. i'll pull logs for rr-6b2f51f2. tim can you grab the auth service logs for that request id and check which key id was presented and its scope?

tim (sre): on it. pulling logs... quick note: if the token is a service key created under a project, it will be rejected for org-scoped endpoints. sending logs in a sec.

infra-bot: log lookup complete for rr-6b2f51f2 — key_id=sk_8c7a (project), org_id=org_123 (owner org), attempted_org=org_911, result=403_PERMISSION_MISMATCH

rory (eng-support): that confirms it — token belongs to org_123 and customer is trying to access org_911. two remediation paths: 1) issue an org-scoped key for org_911 or 2) call the endpoint with credentials for org_123 (if intended). please coordinate with the customer's org admin.

jess (customer): customer says they only have the project key and don't have org admin. they'll ask admin to generate org key. meantime is there a temporary workaround?

maya (support): we can create a short-lived repro token scoped to org_911 for debugging if they authorize. ask the admin to approve by replying here or DM me. alternatively we can test with our own internal repro if you can share a minimal request payload.

rory (eng-support): one more note — if they're using a service account from a CI pipeline, sometimes the token in the pipeline is from a different org due to terraform/state drift. ask them to check the config var value in their pipeline.

jess (customer): admin approved — maya to create temp org token.

maya (support): creating temp token now (1h TTL). will DM the token to admin and request a test.

infra-bot: created token temp-sk-xyz TTL=3600 created_by=maya id=tmp_aa12

jess (customer): admin tested with temp token and now returns 200. new request id rr-6b2f63b9. body OK. customer confirmed their automation pipeline was still using old project key. they will rotate to the org key.

maya (support): excellent. closing loop: root cause = project-scoped key used against org-scoped endpoint (org mismatch). remediation = rotate pipeline to org-scoped key or use project endpoints. if you want, we can provide a checklist for key rotation. :white_check_mark:

jess (customer): yes please a short checklist would be great. thanks all!

rory (eng-support): checklist (quick):
- identify all places where sk is stored (CI vars, env, vault)
- generate org-scoped key in dashboard
- replace sk in a staging job, run smoke tests, verify x-request-id returns 200
- rotate in prod and remove old key from vault
- monitor for 403 spikes in the next 24h

maya (support): I'll follow up with a doc link and ask customer to confirm once rotation complete. closing this thread after confirm. :handshake:
